title: Sprint Queue UX and decision quality

output.summary: Sprint Queue UX refresh and decision-loop proposal contract cleanup.

approvedChanges.question: Should the Sprint Queue dashboard switch to constrained monochrome/gold terminal theme with segmented trace bars?
approvedChanges.currentState: Dashboard still carries blue/neon Amiga-style styling and trace content can exceed viewport width.
approvedChanges.desiredState: Dashboard chrome uses black, white, gray, and gold; traces stay within viewport width; color appears only inside segmented trace bars rendered as 100 one-percent blocks.
approvedChanges.rationale: Old-school terminal feel should come from layout, type, contrast, and blocky bars, not blue backgrounds or neon highlights.
approvedChanges.userImpact: Users get clearer Sprint Queue and decision workflow.
approvedChanges.routeRationale: Approved direction affects product/system behavior and should route through Planning.
approvedChanges.recommendationRationale: User approved direction and change removes confusing internals.

agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Improves trace-first observability and loop discipline.

approvedChanges.rationale: One compact command-center header keeps traces immediately visible and turns summary boxes into useful controls.

approvedChanges.question: Should trace detail open inline as a modern dropdown beneath the clicked trace?

approvedChanges.question: Should user-facing completed trace status consolidate done, closed, and archived into archived?
approvedChanges.currentState: User-facing summary can distinguish done, closed, and archived even though a trace is only truly done when retained/archived.
approvedChanges.desiredState: Dashboard deprecates done and closed as user-facing terminal buckets and uses archived for completed retained traces; technical trace_close remains internal.
approvedChanges.rationale: Archived is the only meaningful user-facing terminal state because completion should imply durable retention.
approvedChanges.userImpact: Users get clearer Sprint Queue and decision workflow.

approvedChanges.question: Should agent/user brainstorming be treated as Decision-loop proposal work with enforced presentation quality before append?
approvedChanges.currentState: Brainstorming can happen as freeform chat, so agents may produce ad hoc proposal formats that bypass agreed Decision-loop format and quality standards.
approvedChanges.desiredState: Brainstorming that affects product/system direction creates or uses a trace, renders candidate Proposed Changes as Sprint Proposal cards, checks Decision-loop quality standards, asks hardening questions for blind spots, and appends only after explicit user approval of the rendered proposal.
approvedChanges.rationale: Making brainstorming proposal work prevents drift before planning.
approvedChanges.userImpact: Users get clearer Sprint Queue and decision workflow.

qualityStandards.description: Sprint Proposal has at least one approved change and stable change ids.
Approved changes provide current state, desired state, and rationale fields for the user intention.
Approved changes explain how the intention benefits users or improves user outcomes.
Approved changes expose maintainer impact and a bounded effort estimate for later semantic cost review.
Approved changes classify work scale and choose micro or standard planning before planning handoff.
Approved changes choose an explicit next loop; direct implementation is limited to low-risk scoped work with validation.
The agent gives a clear approve/reject/defer/ask-user recommendation and explains why approved changes should proceed.
The agent records its judgment that the user's intention is aligned with real user value and project interests.
Independent judge verifies the decision intent is specific, coherent, and sufficient for planning rather than fluent but vague.
Independent judge verifies effort, maintainer impact, work scale, and desired outcome form a plausible cost tradeoff.
Independent judge verifies declared risk tier and route are plausible for the affected scope and authority needs.
High-risk approved changes have explicit user approval authority and a canonical approval ref.
Current state is grounded in canonical source, KB, trace, Git, digest, or test refs.
Decision evidence is sufficient for planning to trust the intention, including stronger proof for high-risk changes.
Approved changes declare a valid risk tier; high-risk intentions identify affected layers and alternatives before implementation work is planned.
Approved changes do not conflict with active trace goals unless the conflict is resolved.
Knowledge impact is recorded as updated refs or explicit no-impact rationale.
Approved changes classify the decision kind so kind-specific quality can apply inside the decision loop.
Improvement decisions describe current pain, desired outcome, success signal, and non-goals.

workItems.title: Implement Sprints Queue dashboard UX refresh
workItems.outcome: Dashboard uses one project header, monochrome/gold terminal chrome, segmented 1% trace bars, filterable summary metrics, search, and inline trace detail expansion.
technicalRequirements: Constrain dashboard layout and trace cards to viewport width with no horizontal overflow.
Replace blue/neon chrome with black, white, gray, and gold; reserve status color for trace bars only.
Render trace progress as 100 one-percent blocks in dashboard state/UI.
Use one header containing project name, summary filters for traces/active/blocked/archived, and search.
Expand exactly one trace inline below the clicked trace and push later traces down.
Expose archived as the terminal summary bucket while preserving internal trace_close semantics.
acceptance: Dashboard has no duplicate system summary header or separate trace detail panel.
Metric boxes filter traces and combine with search.
Trace bars render 100 small blocks and keep color inside bars.
Clicking a trace opens inline detail below that trace; clicking another moves the expanded detail.
Dashboard state exposes archived rather than closed/done as the user-facing terminal bucket.

acceptanceCriteria.text: At narrow and wide viewport sizes, dashboard content remains within the screen and chrome uses only black, white, gray, and gold outside trace bars.
Header shows project name, traces, active, blocked, archived, and search; metric clicks filter traces with visible active state.
Each trace bar is rendered from 100 one-percent blocks with status color applied only inside the bar blocks.
Trace detail expands inline below the selected trace and list layout reflows without a separate side panel.

planningAssessment.rightSizing: One cohesive dashboard UX pass; split would create conflicting edits in the same inline HTML asset.
planningAssessment.independence: Worker can implement using decision refs, dashboard state/model files, and runtime dashboard tests.
planningAssessment.implementationReadiness: Acceptance criteria map to concrete UI state, CSS/DOM behavior, and smoke tests.
planningAssessment.uncertaintyResolution: User approved archived terminology and one-expanded-trace default.
planningAssessment.rationale: Dashboard UX work is self-contained in dashboard state/assets plus focused tests.

resolutions.rationale: Clean change naming and Sprint Proposal card rendering were implemented before dashboard planning resumed.

qualityStandards.description: Every accepted decision ref is covered by a work unit or explicit resolution.
Each work item has enough bounded context to be claimed by one implementation worker.
Each work item breaks decision intent into concrete technical requirements.
Each work item has stable acceptance criteria and verification refs or commands.
Each work item declares standard or micro planning depth; micro-plans stay dependency-free and cover one decision.
Each work item declares worker profile and agent judgment that the unit is independent and implementation-ready.
Independent judge verifies each work unit is atomic enough for one implementation worker and is not a disguised sprint.
Independent judge verifies acceptance criteria and verification commands are concrete enough to prove implementation completion.
Independent judge verifies path scopes and dependencies are no broader than needed for the accepted decisions.
No unresolved planning uncertainty remains; decision or user authority is routed instead of leaking into implementation.
Each work unit is neither sprint-sized nor tiny busywork; sprint remains a grouping or claim batch.
Component refs, path scopes, and verification refs align with source ownership contracts.
Dependencies are known, acyclic, and order overlapping work before implementation.
Recurring, triggered, or hook-based work has a complete planned trigger before runtime can start runs from it.
Planning resolutions use a known kind, carry required evidence, and route-back resolutions return to decision authority before implementation.
Planning refs are canonical trace, KB, Git, digest, source, or test refs.
